title: Adaptive Stopping for Multi-Turn LLM Reasoning
abstract: The paper develops a multi-turn conformal-prediction framework that allocates error budgets across sequential reasoning steps and supports early stopping in settings including adaptive RAG and ReAct while maintaining an overall coverage target.

title: Agent-Orchestrated Adaptive RAG: A Comparative Study on Structured and Multi-Hop Retrieval
abstract: This study evaluates an agentic RAG architecture using dynamic query decomposition, iterative retrieval, and a bounded self-reflective evaluation loop, including experiments on a domain-specific DevOps knowledge base and multi-hop QA.

title: When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs? Bounds, Impossibility, and Adaptation for Structured Generation
abstract: The paper derives limits on conformal risk control for structured LLM generation, including conditions requiring abstention when base risk is too high, and examines adaptive conformal procedures under cross-dataset distribution shift.

title: Do LLMs Know When Evidence is Insufficient? An Evidence Sufficiency Benchmark for Answer-Abstention Calibration in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: The benchmark evaluates whether RAG systems appropriately answer or abstain under full, partial, irrelevant, absent, and conflicting evidence, directly probing calibration to evidence sufficiency rather than ordinary answer accuracy alone.

title: RAG Meets Temporal Graphs: Time-Sensitive Modeling and Retrieval for Evolving Knowledge
abstract: Temporal GraphRAG represents timestamped relations explicitly so identical facts at different times remain distinct, supports incremental corpus updates, and dynamically retrieves subgraphs constrained by both temporal and semantic query scope.

title: Entropic Claim Resolution: Uncertainty-Driven Evidence Selection for RAG
abstract: The method sequentially selects atomic evidence claims according to expected uncertainty reduction and terminates acquisition at an explicit epistemic-sufficiency condition, connecting retrieval selection with a value-of-information style stopping rule.

title: RAG-on-a-Diet: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamic Resource Optimization Framework for RAG
abstract: RAG-on-a-Diet uses reinforcement learning to make per-hop resource decisions from entity and confidence features under a cost-aware objective, with explicit termination based on a hop bound and confidence gate and evaluation that includes out-of-domain data.

title: PromptShift-CRC: Drift-Aware Conformal Risk Control for Foundation Models Under Prompt and Domain Shift
abstract: PromptShift-CRC detects distributional drift and adapts conformal risk-control calibration through reweighting, recentering, and online risk updates, explicitly studying degradation of static calibration under prompt and domain shift.

title: Baikal: Structured Search for Deep Research over Data Lakes
abstract: Baikal casts deep research over heterogeneous data lakes as budgeted search over semantic evidence regions, generating region-grounded subquestions and using value estimates to adaptively balance exploration and exploitation under a fixed investigation budget.

title: Temporal Conjunctive Query Answering via Rewriting
abstract: This work formalizes temporal conjunctive query answering and rewrites structured conjunctions into temporal-logic queries, providing a mechanism for expressing multi-entity joins together with explicit temporal constraints.

title: TimelyRAG: Semantic-Temporal Hybrid Retrieval for Time-Critical Question Answering in Overlapping-Evolving Documents
abstract: TimelyRAG addresses corpora such as laws and policies where amendments create highly overlapping document versions, combining semantic and temporal ranking so queries retrieve version-appropriate evidence rather than merely the most semantically similar text.

title: Few-Shot Conversational Dense Retrieval
abstract: Introduces ConvDR, which learns contextualized dense representations for conversational retrieval and is designed to retain informative prior context while suppressing irrelevant dialogue history.

title: SeaKR: Self-aware Knowledge Retrieval for Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Uses uncertainty in model internal states to trigger retrieval, reranks retrieved knowledge according to uncertainty reduction, and supports repeated retrieval when current evidence remains inadequate.

title: S2G-RAG: Structured Sufficiency and Gap Judging for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented QA
abstract: Introduces an explicit controller that judges whether accumulated evidence is sufficient and, when it is not, emits structured descriptions of the missing evidence; those gap items become the next retrieval query, while a compact evidence context limits accumulation of irrelevant text.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Defines and studies whether retrieved context contains enough information to answer a question, develops context-sufficiency classification, and examines selective answering and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces active retrieval during generation, including FLARE, which anticipates upcoming content and triggers retrieval when generation confidence indicates that additional external evidence is needed.

title: When Should Multi-Round RAG Stop? Structured Stopping Judgments and Retrieval Reduction in Search-R1
abstract: Treats multi-round retrieval stopping as a sequential decision and applies structured sufficiency-and-gap judgments to decide the first state at which retrieval should terminate rather than relying only on a fixed search budget.

title: Beyond Single-Shot: Multi-step Tool Retrieval via Query Planning
abstract: Models retrieval as iterative query planning, decomposing a complex request into successive retrieval queries rather than treating source selection as a single-shot ranking problem.

title: CORAL: Adaptive Retrieval Loop for Culturally-Aligned Multilingual RAG
abstract: Iteratively selects a retrieval corpus, retrieves evidence, critiques its relevance and alignment, checks sufficiency, and, when evidence is insufficient, changes the corpus selection and rewrites the retrieval query.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
abstract: Introduces IRCoT, which interleaves reasoning and retrieval so later retrieval queries are conditioned on facts and intermediate conclusions obtained earlier in the evidence chain.

title: CONQRR: Conversational Query Rewriting for Retrieval with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Trains conversational query rewriting directly against retrieval rewards, connecting contextual resolution to whether downstream evidence can actually be retrieved rather than optimizing rewriting alone.

title: Temporal profiles of queries
abstract: Models temporal profiles of queries and retrieved material, supporting retrieval systems that need to reason about how relevance and information demand vary over time.

title: Improving search relevance for implicitly temporal queries
abstract: Addresses queries whose temporal intent is implicit and develops retrieval methods that incorporate temporal evidence when ordinary topical matching does not fully capture the user's information need.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models
abstract: Models a language model's changing information needs during generation to determine both when retrieval should occur and what query should be issued for the missing information.

title: AB-RAG: Adaptive Budgeted Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Question Answering
abstract: Estimates answer confidence from model certainty, evidence agreement, and retrieval-score variation, then chooses whether to stop or retrieve additional evidence subject to an explicit retrieval budget.

title: Know Before You Fetch: Calibrated Retrieval-Budget Allocation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Formulates adaptive RAG as calibrated allocation among closed-book answering, compact retrieval, larger retrieval, and abstention, explicitly exposing retrieval budget together with latency and token-cost trade-offs.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
abstract: Introduces self-ask, in which a model generates follow-up questions during multi-step reasoning and can send those questions to an external search system, providing a transferable mechanism for deciding the next evidence request.

title: Permission-Aware RAG: Identity and Access Management (IAM)-Based Access Filtering in Multi-Resource Environments
abstract: Enforces resource-level authorization during RAG by validating access in real time against the native IAM systems of independently governed sources, preserving their authorization boundaries instead of merging all policies into a common retrieval store.

title: TASR: Training-Free Adaptive Stopping for Iterative Retrieval
abstract: Proposes a training-free stopping rule for iterative retrieval that combines normalized answer stability with an isotonically calibrated logit-margin signal. The rule is evaluated across multiple models, retrievers, corpora, and dense-retrieval settings with calibration held fixed across extensions.

title: Stop-RAG: Value-Based Retrieval Control for Iterative RAG
abstract: Models iterative RAG as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and learns a value-based controller that chooses whether further retrieval is useful or the system should stop. It directly compares adaptive stopping with fixed-iteration and prompting-based stopping baselines.

title: Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets
abstract: Develops risk-controlling prediction sets with anytime-valid guarantees under sequential and adaptive data collection. It also considers active labeling under a fixed resource budget, making it relevant to controllers that gather evidence adaptively.

title: CLEAR: Cross-Source Evidence Adjudication for Large Language Models in Medicine
abstract: Combines parametric knowledge, curated local sources, and dynamically retrieved evidence, then jointly assesses candidate answers, supporting evidence, provenance, source quality, agreement, and conflict. Unresolved conflicts trigger targeted follow-up search and another adjudication round, making the framework relevant to explicit failure-driven evidence acquisition.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Treats evidence sufficiency as a set-level property rather than independent passage relevance. It aggregates coverage, relation strength, disagreement, conflict, and retrieval uncertainty into support, refute, or insufficient decisions and supports selective answering with calibrated risk.

title: Privacy-provisioned-permission-aware RAG in cloud using identity and access management, trust and large-language models (PPPARITL)
abstract: Integrates identity and access management, role-resource-action-condition authorization, trust scoring, and permission-aware retrieval for enterprise RAG. Candidate material is authorized before similarity ranking, and the architecture also protects embeddings and supports revocation of malicious users.

title: MRAG: A Modular Retrieval Framework for Time-Sensitive Question Answering
abstract: Introduces a temporal RAG evaluation setting and a modular framework that separates semantic content from temporal constraints. Retrieval and ranking combine semantic and temporal relevance to improve answering of time-sensitive questions.

title: Challenges in Information-Seeking QA: Unanswerable Questions and Paragraph Retrieval
abstract: Analyzes unanswerable information-seeking questions and distinguishes failures caused by paragraph retrieval from failures of answerability prediction. The analysis includes retrieval misses and questions requiring evidence distributed across multiple sources.

title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
abstract: Explicitly represents document evolution with version sequences, content boundaries, and changes, and provides intent-routed retrieval for version filtering and change tracking. It also introduces a benchmark for question answering over evolving document versions.

title: When Should Active RAG Retrieve? A Budget-Aware Evaluation of Utility, Calibration, and Cost
abstract: Recasts active retrieval as utility estimation and evaluates retrieval triggers under explicit budgets, calibration transfer, retrieval harm, and cost. The study shows that nominal thresholds and router rankings can fail to transfer reliably across datasets and budgets.

title: A Consensus Glossary of Temporal Database Concepts
abstract: Establishes consensus definitions for temporal-database concepts, including valid time and transaction time. These definitions provide the semantic basis for bitemporal reasoning and distinguishing effective-time validity from database history.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Generalizes conformal methods to control the expected value of monotone loss functions and discusses extensions involving distribution shift and several forms of risk control. It provides a statistical foundation for bounded-risk selective decisions.

title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
abstract: Extends conformal prediction beyond ordinary exchangeability to covariate-shift settings using importance weighting based on train-test density ratios. It supplies a foundation for calibrated risk treatment when deployment distributions differ from calibration data.

title: HONEYBEE: Efficient Role-based Access Control for Vector Databases via Dynamic Partitioning
abstract: Studies nearest-neighbor retrieval when candidate vectors are subject to role-based permission predicates. It introduces dynamic partitioning intended to enforce authorization while controlling the memory and latency costs of permission-constrained vector search.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data

title: When Iterative RAG Beats Ideal Evidence: A Diagnostic Study in Scientific Multi-hop Question Answering
abstract: Compares no-context, oracle-context, and iterative-RAG conditions for scientific multi-hop QA and diagnoses retrieval coverage, query quality, compositional reasoning, and control calibration. It identifies early-stopping miscalibration and late-hop retrieval failures as continuing controller weaknesses.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Trains a language model to retrieve on demand and emit reflection signals about retrieval relevance, factual support, and generation quality. Retrieval can therefore be skipped or invoked repeatedly rather than being a fixed one-shot operation.

title: Provably Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Proposes an encrypted RAG architecture designed to protect both source content and embeddings while limiting retrieval to authorized entities. The work gives formal confidentiality and integrity arguments together with experimental evaluation.
